Ah, let me explain what I was trying to do, because maybe I shouldn't use the functions in the way I am. I was at the association mapping stage, using scan1snps to generate SNP LOD scores based on whole genome data for the CC founders. When plotting these scores (plot_snpasso), in my case, peak LOD scores for SNP associations are inevitably lower than they are using scan1 on allele probabilities (though it's clear from the online examples that snp scan LOD scores could be higher or lower). So I then wondered how to choose an appropriate LOD threshold for SNP LODs--something that would help you decide which SNPs to highlight, as you've done here:

To generate a permutation threshold for SNPs, I...
Computed SNP probabilities using the genoprob_to_snpprob function (with the allele probabilities as my "genoprobs" data). I assumed the resulting SNP probabilities would reflect the same number of markers per chromosome as in the allele probabilities output (generated with genoprob_to_alleleprob). Instead, as I noted, some markers are eliminated on each chromosome;
Used scan1 to generate a LOD profile for the 2-state SNP data;
Used scan1perms to obtain a distribution of maximum LOD scores from which to compute threshold LOD values. Given the LOD scores in my snp associatin plots, I was surprised that the 95% thresholds were basically no lower than for the results from permutations on allele probabilities... enough so that I'm going to go back and re-run the SNP permutations, even though I can't find any mistakes in the way I coded it.
In the end, all I was looking for was comparable thresholding for the snp association LOD scores and plots as I have for the 8-state founder model. Maybe it's not necessary (i.e., the QTL LOD results are the indicator of which associations are meaningful). Any suggestions are again much appreciated.

Thanks, Karl,
David

It has to do with which SNPs are among the "indexed" set in the snp info
you pass to genoprob_to_snpprob(). The output has as many positions are
there are indexed snps in that snp info.

It's hard to say exactly what's going on without seeing your code (and
possibly data), but it may be that when adjacent giga/megamuga markers
have the same founder strain distribution pattern, only one of the two
gets indexed.

karl

OK, I've basically got this figured out. When you pass a cross2 object to the snpinfo argument in geno_to_snpprob, the function calls drop_markers. drop_markers scans the $founder_geno element of the cross2, removing all markers at which any founder is coded 0. I think 0 means no marker information for that founder (with the other options, 1 and 3, representing the major and minor alleles); please correct me if I'm wrong about that.

So, the difference in markers #s between genotype and allele probabilities, on the one hand, and snp probabilities, on the other, is basically a count of how many markers are not genotyped for at least one founder.

I only noticed the discrepancy because one of the peaks from my scan1 analysis (on allele probabilities) turns out to be located at a marker that is removed by the drop_markers function.

David

messages.body_plain:
Hi r/qtl2 group,
   I am using qtl2 to analyze the data in CC mice. I want to use the H-K regression rather than LMM and LOCO method. When I was using out_snps(). An error occured. It  showed that Error in k[["1"]] : subscript out of bounds. How to fix this? Thanks!
   Best,
            Chenhan

Here are my script in R.
library(qtl2)
message("Write control file")
write_control_file("~/RStudio/RawData/cc/cc.json", crosstype = "risib8",
                   geno_file="cc_geno.csv",
                   founder_geno_file="MMnGM_foundergeno.csv",
                   pheno_file="cc_pheno.csv",
                   pheno_transposed=FALSE,
                   gmap_file="MMnGM_gmap.csv",
                   pmap_file="MMnGM_pmap.csv",
                   crossinfo_file="cc_crossinfo.csv",
                   covar_file="cc_covar.csv",
                   sex_covar="Sex",
                   sex_codes=list(male="male",female="female"),
                   xchr="X",
                   geno_codes=c("A"=1, "B"=3),
                   alleles=LETTERS[1:8],
                   geno_transposed=TRUE,
                   founder_geno_transposed=TRUE,
                   description=paste("Data for Collaborative Cross (CC) lines",
                                     "combine with memory data"),
                   overwrite=TRUE)
# create zip file
message("Create zip file")
zip_datafiles("~/RStudio/RawData/cc/cc.json", overwrite=TRUE)
# read data
cc <- read_cross2("~/RStudio/RawData/cc/cc.zip")

# Calculating genotype propabilities
map <- insert_pseudomarkers(cc$gmap, step=1)
# use calc_genoprob() to calculate the QTL genotype probabilities.
pr <- calc_genoprob(cc, map, error_prob=0.002)
# convert genotype probabilities to allele probabilities
apr <- genoprob_to_alleleprob(pr)
# Calculating a kinship matrix
kinship <- calc_kinship(pr)
#SNP association already calculated genotype probabilitie, convert them to allele probabilities
k <- calc_kinship(apr)

#In a QTL scan of the X chromosome, special covariates (such as sex) may need to be included under the null hypothesis of no QTL, to avoid spurious evidence of linkage.
Xcovar <- get_x_covar(cc)
# perform a genome scan, using H-K regression
out <- scan1(pr, cc$pheno, Xcovar=Xcovar)
# plot the LOD curves
par(mar=c(5.1, 4.1, 1.1, 1.1))
ymx <- maxlod(out) # overall maximum LOD scored
plot(out, map, lodcolumn=1, col="slateblue", ylim=c(0, ymx*1.02))
legend("topleft", lwd=0.5, col="slateblue", colnames(out), bg="gray90")

#a plot of the LOD scores, by Haley-Knott regression and the linear mixed model using either the standard kinship matrix or the LOCO method.
# LMM method
out_pg <- scan1(pr, cc$pheno, kinship, Xcovar=Xcovar)
# LOCO method
kinship_loco <- calc_kinship(pr, "loco")
out_pg_loco <- scan1(pr, cc$pheno, kinship_loco, Xcovar=Xcovar)
color <- c("slateblue", "violetred", "green3")
par(mar=c(4.1, 4.1, 1.6, 1.1))
ymx <- max(maxlod(out), maxlod(out_pg), maxlod(out_pg_loco))
for(i in 1) {
  plot(out, map, lodcolumn=i, col=color[1], main=colnames(cc$pheno)[i],
       ylim=c(0, ymx*1.02))
  plot(out_pg, map, lodcolumn=i, col=color[2], add=TRUE)
  plot(out_pg_loco, map, lodcolumn=i, col=color[3], add=TRUE, lty=2)
  legend("topleft", lwd=2, col=color, c("H-K", "LMM", "LOCO"), bg="gray90", lty=c(1,1,2))
}

#create a numeric covariate for sex
sex <- (cc$covar$Sex == "male")*1
names(sex) <- rownames(cc$covar)

##SNP associations
peak_Mbp <- max(out, cc$pmap)$pos
# create a function for querying the CC variants, call create_variant_query_func() with the path to the cc_variants.sqlite file:
query_variants <- create_variant_query_func("~/RStudio/RawData/CCdb/cc_variants.sqlite")

variants <- query_variants(1, peak_Mbp - 1, peak_Mbp + 1)
pmap <- interp_map(map, cc$gmap, cc$pmap)
out_snps <- scan1snps(pr, pmap, cc$pheno, k[["1"]], sex, query_func=query_variants,
                      chr=1, start=peak_Mbp-1, end=peak_Mbp+1, keep_all_snps=TRUE)
#error: Error in k[["1"]] : subscript out of bounds
